searchResults.name: Snow Lake Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description:
Starting at the Alpental Ski Area and leading up to the incredible Snow Lake, this is one of the most popular hikes in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. The route starts by climbing alongside the South Fork Snoqualmie River with Snoqualmie Mountain on your right. You’ll pass by numerous waterfalls and follow steep switchbacks on your way up to the destination.

Start your journey at the parking lot next to the Snow Lakes Trailhead, about 1.5 miles north of the freeway exit for Snoqualmie Pass. The...

searchResults.name: Lake 22 Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description:
Lake Twenty-Two Trail is a beautiful hike to an alpine lake through old-growth forests ending with stunning mountain views of Mount Pilchuck. The trail can be accessed off of Mountain Loop Highway in the North Cascades area of Washington. The trailhead is located east of Granite Falls. 

The path starts out gently enough on a dirt staircase through lush rainforest. You will hear flowing water from Twenty-Two Creek along the way. A bridge crosses the creek around a mile in where there is a...

searchResults.name: Annette Lake Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description:
This trail is well-maintained, features a gentle but steady incline, and has a lot of varying scenery. The first portion of the trail can be muddy alongside waterfalls to get to the Annette Lake trailhead. A series of switchbacks through an old-growth forest make for a fun climb with beautiful views and stunning avalanche chutes.

In the winter months, bringing special equipment such as spikes or waterproof shoes is recommended. It’s a beautiful winter wonderland with lots of snowpacks in...

searchResults.area_name: West Tiger Mountain Natural Resource Conservation Area
searchResults.name: Poo Poo Point Trail
searchResults.location_label: West Tiger Mountain Natural Resource Conservation Area, Washington
searchResults.description:
Poo Poo Point Trail is a popular destination in the Tiger Mountain State Forest, located in the Issaquah Alps. On the shoulder of West Tiger Mountain, this trail reaches heights that come with great views of Mount Rainier, particularly at sunset! The point is a popular launching pad for paragliders and hang gliders. It is also a perfect spot for a picnic at one of the many picnic tables. 

Note that the mapped route on this page is not the most popular approach to Poo Poo Point. This route...

searchResults.name: Margaret's Way Trail to Debbie's View
searchResults.description:
Beginning from the Squak Mountain Lodge, the trail heads through the parking and camping area using old access and logging roads before becoming a true trail. Roads once laced the upper reaches of the mountain, but these are now mostly overgrown with moss-laden bigleaf maple, cedar, western hemlock, and a few Douglas-fir, thanks in part to MacLeod's work to preserve this area. 

Once you step onto the trail itself, you'll wind your way along a hillside, continuing on a moderate grade through...

searchResults.name: Lower Lena Lake Trail
searchResults.description: This is a nice trail in Olympic National Forest with a moderate climb up to Lake Lena. Dogs are allowed but cannot go on the trail to Upper Lake Lena, as it is part of Olympic National Park, and dogs are not allowed on trails in the national park. Expect company as it is a very popular trail. You will need a recreation pass to park at the trailhead.

searchResults.name: Longview Peak and Far Country Lookout Loop
searchResults.location_label: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, Washington
searchResults.description: This loop starts and ends at the Sky Country trailhead via several trails in the central part of Cougar Mountain. First, you will hike up to Shy Bear Pass, then head towards the Doughty Falls Viewpoint. Coal Creek Falls is also along the loop. The falls are best viewed during the spring; by late summer, they often dry up. There are several connecting trails, so it is recommended to download the route beforehand.

searchResults.name: Lake Valhalla Trail
searchResults.description: This trail takes you to a beautiful alpine lake. The trail is steep in the beginning, but becomes more gradual as you get closer to the lake. Bring your swimsuit and a lunch and spend the afternoon taking in the scenery and enjoying the lake. The mosquitoes are known to be bad in the early summer, so bring bug spray.

searchResults.area_name: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area
searchResults.name: Teneriffe Falls Loop via the Mount Teneriffe Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area, Washington
searchResults.description: On the way up, you will hike through the forest filled with moss-covered trees and cross several small streams cascading down the mountain. As you make your way up the rocky switchbacks leading to the falls, you'll come to a nice viewpoint. On the descent, you will cross a scree field that offers more views before entering back into the woods.

searchResults.name: Mount McCausland Trail
searchResults.description:
Starting at the Smithbrook trailhead,  you arrive at a junction with the Pacific Crest Trail after about a mile.

Turn left (southbound) on the PCT on a relatively flat section. About 2 1/2 miles from the trailhead you'll find a turn-off for Mt. McCausland on your right. The trail is unmarked. If you see Lake Valhalla on your left, you have gone too far. The trail to Mount McCausland starts out gentle but the middle section is very steep. You gain 650 feet in about half a mile. There is a...

searchResults.name: Boulder River Trail
searchResults.description:
The Boulder River Trail leads to an unnamed waterfall, a feature that may be considered notable for its height and beauty. The trail itself offers a relatively easy path, but reaching the base of the falls involves a section that requires navigating steeper terrain. 

Those planning to visit should note that the route to the trailhead may be challenging; a high-clearance vehicle is recommended for navigating the road. The trail allows for an experience of natural beauty, culminating in views...

searchResults.name: Debbie's View via May Valley Loop and West Peak Trail
searchResults.description: This route starts from the state park's parking lot, passes the May Valley Loop, Bullitt Gorge, West Peak, Premier Loop trails, and the must-go Debbie's View, which is the only awesome lookout of the whole Squak Mountain.

searchResults.name: Tipsoo Lake to Dewey Lake Loop
searchResults.description:
A beautiful hike with minimal elevation gain around Naches Peak with an option to visit Dewey Lake.

This is a great trail that is perfect for the family within Rainier National Park.  It will take you from Tipsoo Lake with its great view of Mt. Rainier around Naches Mountain in a loop hike with many spectacular views.  On the opposite side of Naches Peak from the highway you will have the option at a junction to visit two more alpine lakes if you have the energy for the descent down to them...

searchResults.name: Sourdough Gap via Pacific Crest Trail
searchResults.description:
This trail takes you through forest to an alpine lake and provides great views of Mt. Adams, Hood, St Helen’s and Rainier.

Dogs aren’t allowed past Sourdough Gap as the trail enters the National Park and pets are not allowed past that point. You can take them on the trail to the boundary but you wouldn’t be able to go all the way to Crystal Lake. However, this isn't the best trail for dogs as it is rocky and hot.

searchResults.name: Striped Peak Loop
searchResults.description: Gorgeous old-growth forest trail with glimpses of the water. The elevation is a bit of a roller coaster, and the trail does get slippery when it’s raining. Trekking poles and sturdy footwear are recommended. This is a very quiet and beautiful trail. Bug spray is recommended during the summer months.

searchResults.name: Deer Lake Trail
searchResults.description: Make sure to check the conditions of roads and facilities before you visit at the National Park Service's website https://www.nps.gov/olym/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

searchResults.name: Eightmile Lake Trail
searchResults.description: This is a beautiful and popular trail that takes you to an alpine lake. It is a steady climb all the way to Eightmile Lake. It is a little overgrown in some places, and then it opens up into beautiful meadows. There is little shade along the way, so come prepared with sun protection and plenty of water. There are great views of Dragontail to the left in the beginning. Keep an eye out for wildflowers blooming in the spring and early summer.

searchResults.name: Fred's Railroad and Wilderness Peak Loop
searchResults.location_label: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, Washington
searchResults.description:
This beautiful and varied trail is perfect for hiking and running, though it can sometimes be steep. Starting from the Sky Country Trailhead, the route includes the Oldman's Trail, Fred's Railroad Trail, and Wilderness Peak.

 Most of the trails are shaded, and there are no real viewpoints. The path offers a mix of wide dirt paths, single track, and metal grate duckboards. However, be cautious, as sections of the trail can become muddy after rain, potentially causing puddles and wet...

searchResults.name: Silver Peak Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description: This demanding summit trek requires negotiating exposed Class 3 scrambling and navigating fields of shifting rock and scree near the peak. The route begins easily enough along the famed Pacific Crest Trail before quickly turning into a steep, rugged boot path that gains most of the elevation rapidly. Near the summit, hikers must be prepared for a taxing scramble that calls for confident footing and the use of hands. The reward for the climb is an unparalleled 360-degree panorama of the...

searchResults.name: Green Mountain via Davis and Gold Creek Trail
searchResults.description:
This loop through Green Mountain State Forest combines Gold Creek, Davis Trail (GM-6), and a logging road (GM-17), with a summit of Green Mountain along the way. There's a stunning view from the top.

Most of the trails are well maintained; however, there are stretches that contain a lot of gravel, which can be slippery. There are many trails in the park, so keep an eye on the map to stay on the correct route.

searchResults.name: Dewey Lake Trail
searchResults.description: This trail goes along the PCT to Dewey lake. Camping is allowed with a self issued wilderness permit at the trailhead. This trail briefly enters Mount Rainier National Park, and dogs are only allowed on the PCT within the park boundaries.

searchResults.name: Maiden Peak from Deer Park Campground
searchResults.description:
The hike begins at the Deer Park Trailhead, which provides parking and restrooms. The road to the trailhead is a rough, unpaved road. The trail follows the Obstruction Point-Deer Park Trail around Green Mountain to the summit of Maiden Peak. The first three-quarters of the hike is through the forest, while the last part takes you through meadows with panoramic views of the valley and mountains. 

You'll encounter incredible scenery, including forests, meadows, alpine views, and larger...

searchResults.name: Mirror Lake via Pacific Crest Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description: Mirror Lake via the Pacific Crest Trail offers a scenic trek through the dense forests of the Snoqualmie Pass region. This route traverses a well-maintained section of the historic Pacific Crest Trail, leading hikers past seasonal ponds and through groves of noble fir and mountain hemlock. While the path is generally easy to follow, be prepared for a rocky and rooty tread that requires steady footwork, especially on the descent. The destination is a crystal-clear alpine lake tucked beneath...

searchResults.name: Central Peak, West Peak, and Debbie's View Loop
searchResults.description:
It is a beautiful hike with a challenging climb to the destination. Looking out from Debbie's View makes the whole hike worthwhile, with expansive panoramic views from the Cascades to Tacoma!

Make sure to have this trail map downloaded, as the area has many intersecting trails.

searchResults.name: Whitaker Peak and Shy Bear Loop Trail to Doughty Falls
searchResults.location_label: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, Washington
searchResults.description:
This trail begins with a steep climb to Whitaker Wilderness Peak, the highest point in Cougar Mountain Park. Although the summit doesn't offer views due to dense vegetation, there’s a giant wooden chair for relaxation. The trail leads through a beautiful shaded forest with ferns and large Douglas fir trees.

The trail continues to Shy Bear Pass and Doughty Falls Viewpoint. During most summer and fall days, the waterfall is barely a trickle over large moss-covered rocks. To see the falls at...

searchResults.name: Perry Creek Falls via Perry Creek Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington
searchResults.description: The Perry Creek Trail travels through the forest with occasional glimpses of the surrounding towering peaks. After about a mile the trail begins to climb uphill and crosses several smaller streams that flow into Perry Creek. Perry Falls is a great place to stop and relax before retracing the route back down.

searchResults.name: Skyscraper Mountain via Sourdough Ridge and Wonderland Trail
searchResults.description:
This is a challenging, yet rewarding hike. The trail follows Sourdough Ridge to the Wonderland Trail and passes Frozen Lake along the way. This is a great trail for viewing wildlife, including mountain goats, bears, marmots, and more.

The views from the top of Skyscraper Peak are breathtaking - mountains as far as you can see! The top of Mt Rainer looks so close you could touch it, and even a view of the Fremont Fire Lookout across the valley.

searchResults.name: Crystal Lake via Sourdough Gap and Sheep Lake
searchResults.description:
While the majority of this trail is within Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, the trail crosses into Mount Rainier National Forest just before Crystal Lake. Those who are planning to camp overnight at Crystal Lake will be required to obtain a wilderness permit from Mount Rainier National Park. 

Dogs are allowed on the trail until you reach Sourdough Gap, where you will enter the Rainier portion of the trail. Dogs are not allowed there, so if you want to reach Upper Crystal Lake, you'll have...

searchResults.name: Berkeley Park Trail
searchResults.description:
Berkeley Park is a lovely meadow alongside Lodi Creek. This trail begins at the Sunrise Visitor Center and follows the Sourdough Ridge Trail to Frozen Lake. From there, follow the Wonderland and Northern Loop Trail to Berkeley Park. Enjoy beautiful views of Mount Rainier and the subalpine landscape.

This is one of Mount Rainier National Park's many backpacking routes. A wilderness permit is required for all overnight stays in the backcountry. A climbing permit is required for all travel...

searchResults.name: Reflection Lakes via Mazama Ridge Loop
searchResults.description: This trail begins from the Paradise Inn area and follows the Skyline, Golden Gate, Mazama Ridge, Wonderland, and Lower Lakes Trail to create a beautiful loop. Views include waterfalls, meadows, wildflowers, lakes, and peaks in the distance. On a clear day, Mount Rainier is towering above everything else, creating a breathtaking backdrop.

searchResults.name: Palisades Lakes Trail
searchResults.description:
This is a quiet trail that takes you past multiple alpine lakes, ending at Upper Palisades Lake. There are beautiful wildflowers in the early summer and many opportunities to see wildlife, including elk and bears. Enjoy beautiful views of lakes, meadows, and the surrounding mountains.

This is one of Mount Rainier National Park's many backpacking routes. A wilderness permit is required for all overnight stays in the backcountry. A climbing permit is required for all travel above 10,000 feet...

searchResults.name: Owyhigh Lakes
searchResults.description:
This trail is a gorgeous hike to some backcountry lakes. There are many vibrant colors throughout this area - the lakes are a mixture of greens and browns, with very clear water. There are beautiful fall colors during the fall months, and wildflowers in the early summer. The elevation is steady and not too demanding. Keep an eye out for wildlife, including elk, mountain goats, marmots, and more!

Parking is a bit scarce, so be sure to arrive early, especially on weekends and during the busy...

searchResults.name: Shadow Lake via Wonderland Trail
searchResults.description: This trail begins at the White River Campground and follows the Wonderland Trail to Shadow Lake and back. There is a steep climb to Shadow Lake, but the views are well worth the hard effort. Continue on to Glacier Overlook for more beautiful views - especially of the Emmons Glacier. If you are looking for something a little easier, you can also hike to Shadow Lake from the Sunrise Visitor Center.

searchResults.name: Silver Lake Way Trail
searchResults.description: Silver Creek Trailhead is the start of the hike. The first mile or so alternates flat meadows with moderate inclines. The second mile or so consists of moderate incline with very uneven terrain and narrow trail. The third mile or so consists of steep inclines. There is one semi confusing fork in the trail where you come across two trees one says “No” and the other says “God’s Men”, go towards “God’s Men” and then keep right.

searchResults.name: West Elwha River Trail
searchResults.description: Campground closed during winter and early spring. Park at the gate and walk 0.25 miles to trailhead.

searchResults.name: Lake George Trail
searchResults.description:
The trail is mostly a steady incline up an old road that is now closed to traffic. The lake is beautiful, and you can see a real close-up view of Mt. Rainier on a clear day.

Bikes are allowed on Westside Road, but not on any of the side trails. It's possible to bike up to the Lake George Trail junction and then hike the rest of the way to Lake George.

This is one of Mount Rainier National Park's many backpacking routes. A wilderness permit is required for all overnight stays in the...

searchResults.name: Green Mountain via Gold Creek and Wildcat Trails
searchResults.description: Dogs are allowed in Green Mountain State forest and must be kept on leash. Horseback riders may have their dogs off-leash as long as they are under voice command.  This route takes you on a loop that ultimately ends up at the top of Green Mountain where you will find a place to stop and have a picnic while taking in the view.

searchResults.name: Hidden Lake Spur via Palisades Lake Trail
searchResults.description:
If you are looking for a fun and relaxing day hike that truly shows the beauty of the pacific northwest, then this is the hike for you! Plan to arrive early, especially on summer weekends, as the parking to the trailhead is also a highly visited viewpoint of Mount Rainier. This close-up view of the mountain is breathtaking.

The start of the trail has a wonderful view looking down on Sunrise Lake. The terrain is easy on our feet and very well-maintained. The hike in consists of mostly shaded...

searchResults.name: Ohanapecosh and Stafford Falls Trail
searchResults.description: The Ohanapecosh and Stafford Falls Trail in Washington offers a beautiful and scenic hiking experience, featuring stunning forest landscapes, river views, with the highlight being the impressive Stafford Falls. The trail provides a peaceful escape into nature, with some moderate elevation changes. There is so many beautiful spots along this trail its hard to list them all, pack your swimmers if you want a mid hike cool off!

searchResults.name: Aylard Farm, Cabin Point, Babbington Hill and Interior Trail Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail begins from the Aylard Farm Trailhead, which can be accessed by following Becher Bay Road just off of East Sooke Road. Trail with nice ocean views throughout and fresh ocean breeze with access to a sandy beach. 

Visit the multiple viewpoints on this trail such as Beechey Head, Squeaky Point, Alldridge Point, and Cabin Point. Historic petroglyphs can be viewed at Alldridge Point. The historic Cabin Point Trap Shack can be visited and explored near Cabin Point.

 Climb to the top of...

searchResults.name: Cle Elum Ridge via Ewok and Crooked Tree Trail
searchResults.description: This trail takes you up into Roslyn Community Forest to the top of Cle Elum (aka Roslyn) Ridge and back down. The climb up to the ridge is steady and constant, passing a trail section also known as the "Never Ending Climb"! Keep your eye out for deer, elk, black bear, flying squirrels and other wildlife in this beautiful forest of towering Grand Fir and Ponderosa Pines.

searchResults.name: Pike Road, Coast, Parkheights, Interior and Anderson Cove
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail begins from the Pike Road Trailhead, which can be accessed by following Pike Road just off of East Sooke Road. This loop includes coastal trail and a few trails through the forest. Expect large roots and narrow paths at areas along the coast, however, once you’re in the forest it’s mostly clear. The loop can be done in either direction. Enjoy and make sure you wear proper footwear as the rocks are slippery when wet. There are great ocean views!

For more information on East Sooke...

searchResults.name: Anderson Cove, Coppermine, Coast, Parkheights and Bubbington Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts from the Anderson Cove Trailhead that can be accessed from East Sooke Road. 

This trail follows 5 different trails in the park. Throughout this trail you will be surrounded by tall mature trees and beautiful forest. 

You will also reach the coastline where you will have spectacular views of the seascape. Mount Maguire has an excellent viewpoint of whole park and beyond.

searchResults.name: Capitol Peak via Greenline Trail
searchResults.description: Capitol Peak has several approaches, including a fire road, to its summit. This route starts from C-Line Road, and heads north on the Greenline Trail. The singletrack undulates through dense forest and clear cut as it steadily climbs toward Forest Road 4000. Follow the road east to the summit and enjoy the panoramic views from the top.

searchResults.name: Jolly Mountain Trail
searchResults.description:
Amazing gem of a trail! The road to the trailhead is rough and 4WD is recommended. The trail is rocky but well-maintained. There is little shade along the way, which provides plenty of views of the surrounding landscape, including Mount Rainier and Mount Stewart, but also means there is little shelter from the elements. Bring plenty of water, sun protection, and layers. In the early summer, there are beautiful wildflowers that line the trail.

There are a few gates at the beginning of the...

searchResults.name: Mima Falls West Trail
searchResults.description: This route takes you to Mima Falls from the west, which is a less-popular way to access the falls. Mima Falls is the highlight of Capitol State Forest, and is worth visiting if you are in the area. The trails here are not well-marked, so downloading offline maps is recommended. The trail can be muddy at times, so sturdy footwear is recommended.

searchResults.name: Beechey Head, Cabin Point and Babbington Hill Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail begins from the Aylard Farm Trailhead, which can be accessed by following Becher Bay Road just off of East Sooke Road. Light easy trail with nice ocean views throughout and fresh ocean breeze with access to a sandy beach. 

Visit the multiple viewpoints on this trail such as Beechey Head, Cabin Point and the top of Babbington Hill. The trail to Beechey Head is wide, pretty, and quick going. 

There are lots of roots and rocks along the Coast Trail to Cabin Point that make travel...

searchResults.name: Ewok, 4th of July, and Rocky's Loop
searchResults.description: This route takes you on a fun loop through the Roslyn Urban Forest trail system. You'll ascend the ridge via the Ewok Trail, complete the Upper Traverse, then descend via Rocky's Trail. Part of this mapped route travels along roads in the town of Roslyn. The Roslyn Community Trails are planned so that some of the loops do follow roads in town. This is a short section, and the town of Roslyn welcomes hikers, bikers, and runners- but keep your eye out for cars and pedestrians on your route.

searchResults.name: Anderson Cove, Pike Road, Coast and Coppermine Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts from the Anderson Cove Trailhead that can be accessed from East Sooke Road. 

This trail follows four different trails in the park. Throughout this trail you will be surrounded by tall mature trees and beautiful forest. 

You will also reach the coastline where you will have spectacular views of the seascape.

searchResults.name: Coppermine Trail from Anderson Cove Trailhead
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts from the Anderson Cove Trailhead that can be accessed from East Sooke Road. 

This trail follows the Anderson Cove trail and joins Coppermine Trail all the way to the coastline. Throughout the trail, you will be surrounded by tall mature trees and beautiful forest. 

Once you reach the coastline, you will have spectacular views of the seascape. This can be a great spot to stop for a snack before continuing along the trail.

searchResults.name: Endurance Ridge, Parkheights, and Coast Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts off on a steep slope to warm you up. There are lots of large cedars and it's a rocky, rugged trail. The descent to the coastline can be muddy and slippery when wet so appropriate footwear is recommended. 

Following the Endurance Ridge Trail to the first fork, take a right and then a left at the next fork to follow the Parkheights Trail all the way to the coastline. 

Once at the coastline, you will be rewarded with beautiful views of the seascape as you follow the trail...

searchResults.name: Creyke Point, Cabin Point, Babbington Hill and Interior Trail Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail begins from the Aylard Farm Trailhead, which can be accessed by following Becher Bay Road just off of East Sooke Road. Trail with nice ocean views throughout and fresh ocean breeze with access to a sandy beach. 

Visit the multiple viewpoints on this trail such as Creyke Point, Beechey Head, Squeaky Point, Alldridge Point, and Cabin Point. Historic petroglyphs can be viewed at Alldridge Point. The historic Cabin Point Trap Shack can be visited and explored near Cabin Point. Climb...

searchResults.name: Quartz Creek Trail
searchResults.location_label: Mount Baker Snoqualmie National Forest, Washington

searchResults.name: Coast from Copper Mine Road
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
The Coast from Copper Mine Road is really a great trail with amazing views of the seascape. The trail is pretty wide for a good chunk of the hike, but gets a bit narrow and a little overgrown when you hit Coast Trail, the views are well worth it. 

Be cautious on the Coast Trail as it can feel narrow and there is a significant drop. This hike is mostly a decline the whole way and would require two vehicles at either end unless you decide to do this trail as an out and back. 

Really a great...

searchResults.name: Endurance Ridge, Babbington Hill, Coast and Parkheights Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts off on a steep slope to warm you up. Lots of large cedars and rocky, rugged trails. Following the Endurance Ridge Trail to the second fork, take a left to climb Babbington Hill. 

Once at the top, you will be rewarded with vistas of the park from above and the seascape on a clear day. Then follow the the Endurance Ridge Trail all the way to the coastline and you will be rewarded with gorgeous views of the seascape. 

This trail visits the Cabin Point Trap Shack that...

searchResults.name: Gallagher Lake via Fortune Creek Jeep Trail 4W301
Endurance Ridge, Babbington Hill, Coast and Parkheights Extended Loop
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts off on a steep slope to warm you up. Lots of large cedars and rocky, rugged trails. Following the Endurance Ridge Trail to the second fork, take a left to climb Babbington Hill. 

Once at the top, you will be rewarded with vistas of the park from above and the seascape on a clear day. Along the Coast Trail, you will be rewarded with gorgeous views of the seascape. 

This trail visits the Cabin Point Trap Shack that historically used to be the type of shack where watchmen...

searchResults.name: Anderson Cove to Iron Mine Bay from Anderson Cove Trailhead
searchResults.location_label: East Sooke Regional Park, British Columbia
searchResults.description:
This trail starts from the Anderson Cove Trailhead that can be accessed from East Sooke Road. 

This trail follows the Anderson Cove trail and throughout it you will be surrounded by tall mature trees and beautiful forest. There are mild elevations on the trail, but the path is lovely even in the snow.

You will reach the coastline at Iron Mine Bay where you will have spectacular views of the seascape. This can be a great spot to stop for a snack before continuing along the trail.
